name: Book Edge Sweep
rule: Buy the cheaper executable side when its ask is <= 45c and the displayed spread is >= 2c; sell at a bid >= 1.5x entry, else hold to settlement.
why: A return-seeking price dislocation hypothesis that uses only the current Kalshi book. It is not a claim that the dislocation is an arbitrage.
evidence: Kalshi market quote plus a fresh order-book snapshot

name: 24h Momentum
rule: When the last trade is >= 3c away from the last trade a day ago (official previous_price field; market must be >= 24h old), buy that direction at the ask with a +2c limit; sell at a bid 5c above entry, else hold to settlement.
why: A simple momentum hypothesis whose input and date are observable. It can fail when the last trade is stale or liquidity is thin, so a fill is still book-dependent.
evidence: Kalshi last price, previous price, current quote and order book

name: Expiry Tail Sprint
rule: Inside 48h of expected resolution (expected_expiration_time, else close_time), buy any side quoted at or below 15c and hold to official settlement.
why: A deliberately aggressive expiry hypothesis for the return leaderboard. The result must be judged against the official settlement result or a verified exit book, not a guessed outcome.
evidence: Kalshi close time, status, quote and order book

name: Depth Imbalance
rule: When displayed YES vs NO depth imbalance exceeds 35% (both sides present), buy the heavier side and hold to settlement.
why: Tests whether visible depth predicts short-run price movement. It explicitly logs the book levels because displayed liquidity can disappear before a paper fill.
evidence: Kalshi order-book levels and retrieval timestamp

name: Cheap Dip Hunter
rule: Buy any side quoted between 1c and 5c on a market with traded volume; sell at a bid >= 2x entry, else hold to settlement.
why: Return-seeking lottery tickets: pay pennies, need a double or a 100% payoff. The committed tape shows why it bleeds — one-sided books keep the YES bid at zero, so exits never verify and cheap tickets settle at zero.
evidence: data/season-2026/trades.json (dip-hunter rows) · verified candlesticks, no look-ahead

name: Release Spike Surfer
rule: When the 24h move (last trade vs the last trade a day ago) is >= 20c and 24h volume >= 1,000 on a market >= 24h old, buy the direction of the move with a +2c limit; sell at the first bid above entry, else hold to settlement.
why: Chases information releases when the verified tape shows both a jump and heavy official volume. The committed window contained exactly one qualifying spike (the NFL final-drive bar) and it paid; the CPI release spike failed the 3x volume gate, which is the documented trap-avoidance.
evidence: data/season-2026/trades.json (spike-surfer rows) · verified candlesticks, no look-ahead

name: Favorite Holder
rule: Buy a 90-97c favourite (displayed spread <= 5c) on a market with >= 100,000 contracts of volume and hold to settlement.
why: Favorite-longshot-bias play: heavy favorites on event markets are often slightly under-priced. Only enters when the verified tape proves a liquid 90+ cent favorite — in the committed window that happened once (NFL 95 cents) and settled to $1.
evidence: data/season-2026/trades.json (sure-thing rows) · verified candlesticks, no look-ahead

name: Certainty Carry
rule: Buy a 97-99c side (displayed spread <= 5c) on a market with volume whose expected resolution is within 21 days; hold to settlement.
why: Earns the residual on near-certain outcomes with a hard time horizon. The committed tape produced one qualifying bar (CPI, NO ask 0.99, 18.5 days to settlement) that settled to $1 for a small positive PnL; the NFL 32-cent NO ask is correctly rejected as not carry.
evidence: data/season-2026/trades.json (yield-sniper rows) · verified candlesticks, no look-ahead

name: Market-Making Quote Plan
status: Kept gated for ranking: a REST snapshot cannot prove FIFO queue position. Since 2026-09-22 the desk posts its quote plans (status quote_plan) and scripts/maker_model.py matches each posted price against the official trade tape - only a print strictly through the posted price counts as proof of a fill (MODELLED, never a ledger fill).
rule: Place a simulated two-sided quote inside a measured spread and wait for future verified market-data evidence before calling it filled.
why: Tests market-making economics, queue uncertainty and maker-fee differences. A REST snapshot cannot prove queue position or a maker fill, so this roster entry creates plans, not fake fills.
evidence: Kalshi order book plus later verified trade-tape prints

name: Momentum Cross (Pine-style)
rule: Long when last price > slow SMA and fast SMA > slow SMA (daily 5/10, hourly 3/6); exit when last price < slow SMA at the verified bid; else hold to official settlement.
why: Classic trend-following on a verified tape. The committed result shows both failure modes: 1-tick range crosses that stop out against the spread, and the genuine breakout that paid.
